newsitem.title: USA: MobileMedia seeks $200 mln DiP financing OK.
newsitem.headline: MobileMedia seeks $200 mln DiP financing OK.

text.p: MobileMedia Corp said on Thursday it has received a commitment for up to $200 million in debtor-in-possession financing from a consortium of banks led by Chase Manhattan Corp and is seeking the court's permission to access the financing.
The paging company said earlier today it filed for Chapter 11 protection in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Delaware.
MobileMedia said its immediate needs were to satisfy short-term financing requirements, reach an agreement with Motorola Inc, its principal supplier of pagers, and start restructuring.
It also said it hired turnaround consultants Alvarez & Marsal Inc to help implement the restructuring.

MobileMedia said one of the conditions for borrowing under the DiP facility is reaching an agreement with certain key suppliers of paging equipment. The company said it would file a motion seeking to pay the suppliers' pre-petition claims, including Motorola's.
MobileMedia said it believes the court will approve the motion and Motorola will agree to commence shipping product and providing services.
The company said it currently has enough cash to fund operations and pay post-petition obligations to trade suppliers until it expects to reach a pact with Motorola and gain access to the financing.
Also, employees would be paid in the normal course of business during the reorganization proceeding, the company said.

MobileMedia, the second largest provider of paging and personal communications services in the United States, said last month it would have to file for protection if it could not reach an agreement with its creditors and suppliers.
The company's stock was down 3/32 at 7/16 in late-morning trading.
